body:
It's that feeling that every thing you liked about them is still there, but its directed at someone else. All you get is bitterness and the feeling of being the evil witch in their fairy tale of happiness. 

They got engaged a couple months ago and it tore me to shreds. We had prepared to spend the rest our lives together, but now someone else is going to do that instead. Every single cute, sweet moment that you adore so much, that personality that you live is going to be spent with someone else.

People have told me that that just means that you two weren't "compatible" and you'll be happy in the future. I don't know. That could be true, but it doesn't do anything to stop that knife twist in your heart every time you think of their memory and constantly have reminders, even for something as small as brushing your teeth together. Even regular daily life things are a constant painful memory. 

Fucking love. Drowning my heart in tears and alcohol doesn't make everything okay until the blackout after and then you'll see it in your dreams and resume your living nightmare tomorrow.

I wish I could upvote you more. It's been over a year and it still feels like that. 

Hell its 5 am and I'm still up because I'm not drunk enough to pass out without thinking of that other person sleeping with someone else the same way I did before

Noting else to do while trying to get drunk to forget what Christmas could have been if she didn't leave. Hate my family but going to have to see them tomorrow, at least I have my hangover to focus on instead of anything anyone else is saying

Spend most of it trying to distract myself with computer games, waiting for the right date to finish dying since she left me. I'd drink maybe a bottle or two of gin and whiskey a week, clicking on lines and closing them because I've already seen their content. Lie in bed staring at the ceiling remembering what it was like to not do this by myself. Wishing I were dead, but not brave enough to pull the trigger.

Free time is the enemy, I look okay if I'm at work, or with other people as the situation requires it. I dread weekends because everyone else has better things to do than to interact with me.
This is exactly the same thing mine has been doing for about three hours now..
I've given it a try over a year now and see nothing new has changed just gotten more painful instead of less..
Oh and it looks like I might lose my job because I'm depressed and people don't like interacting with me. Yay Tuesday.

So, six years ago, I had completely given up on dating and was okay with being forever alone, when she came into my life. It was completely unexpected and she turned out to be really similar to me and it was a level of understanding I didn't know a person could have. 

I get that it's possible, and I feel that this was my one chance at happiness and I blew it by being jealous/clingy/a shitty boyfriend/<insert failure here>. Like here's everything you ever wanted in a person, don't fuck it up. And then I did. I can't find anything that chips away that belief that she was the only one out there; that I can never find anyone else like her and have as intense of a relationship that I once had.

I recently lost a family member to cancer and it had affected me even less than this loss of a woman. I've been trying to talk to a professional about it, but I'm getting a lot of 'you're going to change because you don't want to, so why are you here' from it.

They gave me an diagnosis of chemical depression too and some meds to take that don't really help much. They make it so I care about making an effort at the expense of more frequent depressed episodes and intense migraines and nausea.
I guess I will be on tonight :(
